query: Arm based hyperscaler CPUs Graviton Grace Axion adoption
normalized: adoption arm axion based cpus grace graviton hyperscaler

output.content:
**Arm hyperscaler-CPU adoption: Graviton is the clear volume leader; Axion is ramping quickly; Grace is principally an AI-system CPU rather than a broad general-purpose cloud-VM franchise.** [[1, 2, 3]]

| Platform | Adoption evidence | Assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **AWS Graviton** | For the third consecutive year, more than half of newly added AWS CPU capacity was Graviton-powered, and 98% of AWS’s top 1,000 EC2 customers had benefited from Graviton; AWS also reports more than 120,000 customers building on Graviton. [[1, 4]]| This is the most mature Arm CPU deployment among hyperscalers, with adoption extending across mainstream cloud-native, database, application, and increasingly agentic-AI CPU workloads. [[4, 5]]|
| **Google Axion** | Google launched its first Axion machine family, C4A, in October 2024, and later stated that more than 40% of its top 100 Compute Engine customers were using Axion while thousands of Google internal applications ran on it. [[6, 2]]| Axion appears to be in a rapid customer and internal-fleet ramp, aided by expansion beyond raw VMs into GKE, Dataproc, Batch, Dataflow, Cloud SQL, and AlloyDB. [[6, 2]]|
| **NVIDIA Grace** | Grace adoption is concentrated in tightly integrated AI infrastructure—GH200 Grace Hopper systems and GB200 Grace Blackwell racks—rather than conventional standalone cloud CPU instances. [[7, 3]]| AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud were identified by NVIDIA as early Blackwell cloud providers, while AWS, Google Cloud, and OCI planned Grace Blackwell-based instances. [[3]]|

**Graviton: broad production standardization at AWS.** AWS’s adoption data indicate that Graviton has crossed from an Arm alternative into a core default procurement choice for incremental CPU capacity, rather than being confined to experimental or specialized instances. [[1]] AWS identifies customers including Adobe, Airbnb, Atlassian, Epic Games, Formula 1, Pinterest, SAP, Siemens, Snowflake, and Synopsys among the top EC2 users that have benefited from Graviton. [[1]] The newest Graviton5/M9g generation extends the platform toward agentic-AI-adjacent CPU work, with 192 cores, larger cache, and lower inter-core latency. [[4]]

**Axion: the strongest evidence of an early Google Cloud adoption curve.** Google says Axion offers up to 65% better price-performance than current-generation x86 instances and up to 10% better performance than leading Arm alternatives, although these are Google-stated comparative figures rather than independently normalized benchmarks. [[2]] Spotify said it was migrating its entire compute infrastructure to Axion, while Google named ClickHouse, Databricks, Elastic, MongoDB, Palo Alto Networks, Redis Labs, and Starburst as ISVs using Axion for data-processing products. [[2]] The January 2026 general availability of the N4A family broadened Axion from the original C4A compute-optimized offer toward a more complete Arm VM portfolio. [[6]]

**Grace: meaningful strategic adoption, but its metric should be AI-rack deployment rather than CPU share.** NVIDIA reported GH200 availability in early access through Lambda and Vultr, OCI plans for GH200 instances, and CoreWeave plans for early GH200 availability, illustrating that early Grace Hopper cloud distribution was more selective than Graviton’s or Axion’s broad VM deployment. [[7]] The subsequent GB200 platform materially expands Grace’s hyperscaler relevance because the NVL72 system combines 72 Blackwell GPUs with 36 Grace CPUs, and major clouds committed to offer the platform. [[3, 8]] NVIDIA also describes major-cloud adoption of Grace Blackwell as supporting AI training, inference, reasoning, and physical-AI workloads, reinforcing that Grace demand is tied to accelerator-centric deployments. [[9]]

**Bottom line for investors:** Graviton is the clearest evidence that Arm can take substantial general-purpose hyperscaler CPU capacity; Axion validates that the model is replicable at Google; and Grace makes Arm strategically important in AI racks even where it does not displace x86 as a broadly selectable standalone cloud CPU. [[1, 2, 3]] The principal adoption watch items are Graviton’s share of AWS incremental capacity, Axion’s expansion from top-customer usage into broader services and regions, and the realized availability and deployment scale of GB200/Grace Blackwell systems at the large clouds. [[1, 2, 3]]
